[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''Nancy Glasgow''' was born about 1810 or 1811. The surviving 1851 mortality schedule records her as a daughter of [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]], aged 36 when she died of dysentery in 1847.<ref name="Kilconway1851">[https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1851censuskilconway.pdf William Macafee and W. Scott, ''1851 Census for some Parishes and Townlands in the Barony of Kilconway, Co. Antrim''], Dunaghy parish, Glenleslie household 21.</ref><ref name="Detailed1851">[https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf ''1851 Irish Census Returns: detailed comma-delimited transcription''], Glenleslie household 21, pp. 103–104.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1022]] is assessed at 99% (proved). The held 1851 Glenleslie household 21 mortality transcription calls Nancy,36, daughter of John Glasgow and dates her death to 1847. This is the exact household represented by John-1022; uncertain maternity does not weaken his recorded father role.

Whole selected father-profile proposition; maternity and upstream ancestry assessed separately.

Next useful test: Compare original household 21 mortality image with both transcriptions.

Source basis already held: [https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf 1851 Irish Census Returns: detailed comma-delimited transcription (https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851 irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf), Glenleslie household 21, pp. 103–104.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


The return names John as Nancy's father but does not identify her mother. John's wife [[Alexander-16967|Rose Alexander]] remains an uncertain mother; no sourced replacement has been found. The mortality entry does not state Nancy's birthplace, so the populated Dunaghy birthplace remains an uncertain family-context estimate rather than a fact from this record.

The household was formerly cited through the [https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Dunaghy/Glenleslie/21/ National Archives of Ireland census item URL]. The detailed and Macafee/Scott transcriptions cited above preserve the household evidence used here.
